sources.title: Evidence-based guideline: premature ovarian insufficiency (ESHRE, ASRM, CREWHIRL and IMS Guideline Group on POI)
sources.claim: POI = loss of ovarian activity before 40; disordered cycles for at least 4 months plus FSH > 25 IU/l; a single FSH test with the clinical picture is enough; prevalence about 1% in older studies to 3.5% in recent ones; hormone therapy recommended until the usual age of menopause and does not affect chances of natural conception; oocyte donation is an established option; no intervention reliably shown to increase ovarian activity and natural conception.
sources.quote: disordered menstrual cycles (spontaneous amenorrhea or irregular menstrual cycles) for at least 4 months, and an elevated FSH concentration > 25 IU/l ... a single FSH assessment in combination with the characteristic clinical picture is now considered sufficient ... varies from approximately 1% in older studies to 3.5% in recent publications ... HT is recommended for women with POI until the usual age of menopause ... oocyte donation is an established option to achieve pregnancy after a diagnosis of POI ... no interventions that have been reliably shown to increase ovarian activity and natural conception rates

sources.title: Resumption of Ovarian Function and Pregnancies in 358 Patients with Premature Ovarian Failure
sources.journal: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism
sources.claim: Of 358 women with idiopathic POI, 86 (24%) showed resumption of ovarian function, mostly within 1 year of diagnosis; 15 women (4.4%) had 21 spontaneous pregnancies and 16 births.
sources.quote: Of 358 patients with idiopathic POF, 86 (24%) patients presented features indicating resumption of ovarian function ... Twenty-one spontaneous pregnancies (16 births, five miscarriages) occurred in 15 (4.4%) patients.

sources.title: Effects of intraovarian injection of autologous platelet rich plasma on ovarian reserve and IVF outcome parameters in women with primary ovarian insufficiency
sources.claim: 311 women with POI (ESHRE criteria, age 24-40) had intraovarian PRP; 23 (7.4%) conceived spontaneously; 201 (64.8%) developed antral follicles and attempted IVF; 25 (8.0%) reached live birth or sustained implantation.
sources.quote: Women (N=311; age 24-40) diagnosed with POI based on ESHRE criteria underwent intraovarian PRP injection ... After PRP injection, 23 women (7.4%) conceived spontaneously ... 201 (64.8%) developed antral follicle(s) and attempted IVF ... 25 (8.0%) achieved livebirth/sustained implantation
sources.checked_with: WebFetch PMC full text (and aging-us.com abstract) 2026-10-19

sources.title: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment of the ovaries significantly improves fertility parameters and reproductive outcomes in diminished ovarian reserve patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: 38 studies, 2,256 women with low ovarian reserve including POI; antral follicle count rose by a mean of 1.60; spontaneous pregnancy proportion 0.07 and live birth 0.11; mostly observational studies of variable quality.
sources.quote: 38 eligible studies were identified reporting on 2256 women ... The antral follicle count elevated significantly MD 1.60 ... spontaneous pregnancy ... 0.07 ... livebirth was 0.11 ... predominantly observational studies of variable quality

sources.title: Hippo signaling disruption and Akt stimulation of ovarian follicles for infertility treatment
sources.claim: In vitro activation (IVA) of ovarian tissue in women with POI: residual follicles were found in ovaries of 13 of 27 patients; a healthy baby was delivered after embryo transfer.
sources.quote: ovaries from 13 of 27 patients contained residual follicles ... Following embryo transfer, a healthy baby was delivered.

sources.title: First live births after adipose-derived stem cells and platelet-rich plasma intraovarian administration
sources.claim: Two women aged 45 and 46 had live births after intraovarian adipose nanofat plus PRP; in one, antral follicle count rose from 2 to 14 and she conceived naturally about six months later. Observational, no control group.
sources.quote: two women aged 45 and older who achieved live births following intraovarian administration ... antral follicle count increased from 2 to 14 ... Six months later, she conceived naturally

sources.title: Premature ovarian insufficiency and infertility
sources.claim: About 5% of women have a spontaneous pregnancy after a POI diagnosis; most need donor eggs; sister donors carry higher cycle cancellation (30.8% vs 6.6% anonymous); fertility preservation for those at risk; psychological support should be offered.
sources.quote: Approximately 5% of women will have a spontaneous pregnancy after a POI diagnosis ... most women with POI will require a donor oocyte/embryo for pregnancy ... using oocyte donation from the sister of a patient with POI unfortunately carries a higher risk of cycle cancellation (30.8% vs 6.6%) ... Psychological support should be offered.

sources.title: Primary Ovarian Insufficiency (MedlinePlus, US National Library of Medicine)
sources.claim: In about 90% of cases the cause of POI is unknown; known causes include Fragile X and Turner syndromes, autoimmune disease, chemotherapy or radiation, and toxins such as cigarette smoke.
sources.quote: In about 90% of cases, the cause is unknown ... genetic disorders (such as Fragile X and Turner syndromes), autoimmune diseases ... chemotherapy or radiation, and exposure to toxins like cigarette smoke

sources.title: What is Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (previously called Premature Ovarian Failure)?
sources.claim: Approximately 10% of women with POI may be able to get pregnant using their own eggs; donor eggs are the most reliable strategy.
sources.quote: approximately 10% of women with POI may be able to get pregnant using their own eggs ... the use of donor eggs is the most reliable strategy to achieve pregnancy
